lines.text: Issue one thirty-three. A relationship was saved in whichever model you drew it from, so a new fact meant editing its dimensions.
Before.
Three models on the canvas, and no relationships yet.
Drag from the customer key to the order's customer column.
The dialog reads it from the dimension: customer is the many side.
Create the relationship.
Now open the dimension's file.
The relationship was written into the dimension's file.
And the fact's file.
The fact file has nothing.
After, with this pull request.
Three models on the canvas, and no relationships yet.
Drag from the customer key to the order's customer column.
The dialog turns it round, and says it will be saved in the fact's file.
Create the relationship.
Now open the dimension's file.
The dimension file is untouched.
And the fact's file.
It lives with the fact, as many to one.
New: a relationship can carry a role, like ship date.
Drag the date key to the ship date column, and name it.
The role is drawn on the line.
And for a project saved by the previous version.
The new check command flags both relationships saved the old way.
A project saved by version 1.6.7, before this change.
The dimension holds the relationship, and its key was flagged as a foreign key.
Open the diagram.
ERD Studio offers to tidy it up. Nothing changes until you confirm.
One preview lists every change, and anything that needs you.
Repaired in one step. The diagram draws the same lines.
Both relationships now live with the fact, as many to one.
And the dimension is back to just its own columns.
After the repair, the check is clean.

Behind the scenes: every part of ERD Studio now agrees on when two relationships are the same. Saving never drops what it could not read, and old files still render. A new check command reports problems with stable codes, and the AI helper files teach the same rules.
Relationships now live with the fact, older projects get a one-step repair, and a link can carry a role.
